title: Cardinal Billing Account Standing Rule: Relief Rate on Additional-Premium Billing Charges
content:
**Rule.** A relief rate multiplies the billing charge of a Cardinal Billing Account additional-premium bill: **0.50** when the most recent payment posted to the account was made by debit card, credit card or bank EFT and no payment on the account was returned in the last 12 whole months; **0.75** when exactly one of those two holds; **1.00** when neither holds.

A window of the last 12 whole months holds every record posted less than 12 whole months before the bill date, counted on calendar months. The most recent payment is the latest payment entry on the account's billing history by posting date; a returned payment is a returned-payment entry on it.

## Truth table

| Most recent payment by debit card, credit card or bank EFT | No returned payment in the last 12 whole months | Relief rate |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 0.50 |
| Yes | No | 0.75 |
| No (check, money order or cashier's check) | Yes | 0.75 |
| No | No | 1.00 |

**Hypothetical cases.** An account whose latest payment was a money order and which has had no returned payment in the window: 0.75. An account whose latest payment was by credit card but which had a payment returned 4 months before the bill date: 0.75. A billing charge of $6.00 at 0.50 becomes $3.00.
